title: OKC: Finals Game 1, 2012
description: A double-digit hole, 36 in the takeover, and one lead change all night—Go Deep into the loudest June Chesapeake ever heard.
imageHint: Chesapeake Energy Arena, June 2012, blue and orange roaring

questions.question: In Game 1 of the 2012 NBA Finals, which Thunder star scored 36—including 17 in the fourth—to beat Miami?
questions.explanation: Twelve-of-twenty from the field at home. Once OKC took the lead late in the third, it never trailed again.

questions.question: Durant's running mate that night nearly had a triple-double with 27 points, 11 assists, and 8 boards—who?
questions.explanation: Westbrook's second-half aggression flipped the game. Three of Durant's late buckets came directly off his dimes.

questions.question: Westbrook's layup-and-one with 16.4 seconds left in the third gave OKC the lead for good against which LeBron–Wade–Bosh franchise?
questions.explanation: LeBron finished with 30. Final: Thunder 105, Heat 94—OKC's first Finals win as a franchise.

questions.question: Before that Heat comeback flip, OKC had trailed by how many points in the first half of Game 1?
questions.explanation: A 13-point hole at home in a Finals opener. The fourth-quarter takeover made the deficit feel like a setup.

questions.question: After climbing out of that 13-point hole, how many lead changes did the entire Game 1 have?
questions.explanation: Box-score trivia locals still cite: once Westbrook put OKC ahead late in the third, the lead never flipped back. One punch. Done.

questions.hint: Clay Bennett, bitter arena fight, Sam Presti already GM

easterEgg.title: The glue guy
easterEgg.text: Nick Collison came off the bench for 10 rebounds and helped own the glass 43–35. Perkins started; the glue guy cleaned up. Locals still cheer the name.
